correctness.rationale: Two sources in one half-open unit cell are less than √2 apart, so they are lattice neighbors; triangle-freeness rules out triple fibers. The positive horizontal and vertical source edges give phase windows [0,1−a/q)×[0,1−b/q) and [b/q,1)×[0,1−a/q). Because a,b are units modulo q and h²=−1 modulo q, the source phases equidistribute on the q elements (r,[hr]_q), with q sources per phase in one q×q source period. Boundary cells along the inverse target square contribute O_q(M), so the double-fiber density is (H+V)/q. Rotation of phases (r,t)↦(−t,r) takes the horizontal points except zero exactly to the vertical points: t=0 forces r=0 and the potentially unmatched endpoint r'=b is excluded since [hb]_q=q−a. Thus V=H−1. The full source count over target squares differs from the number of target cells by O(M), giving equality of the limiting zero- and double-fiber frequencies. For the discrepancy, with q=u²+v² the modular graph lift has vectors (u,v) or (v,u) according to the leg orientation, and their quarter turns. The determinant q equals the lattice index, so their centered square tiles have covering radius ρ=√(q/2). The tile union from each rectangle's lattice centers lies between its erosion and dilation by ρ; the enclosing-box area error is at most 2ρ(w+z)+4ρ², valid also when an eroded side is empty. Summing both errors and dividing by q² gives exactly the stated bound. The triple (3,4,5) has H=1, and the generic continuous benchmark there is 4/25 rather than 1/5.
residual_risks: Fresh integer-floor enumeration checked 36 complete target quotient histograms up to q=145. The quotient is Z²/(qRθ Z²), of size q², and the histogram labels target classes using the two inverse-rotation numerators modulo q². Finite checks do not prove the universal limit or bound.
The exact odd numerator uses floor boundaries; there is no claim for centered rounding of resonant rotations or higher iterates.

Exact raw collision counts by a finite sum can be recovered from those ingredients, so the novelty is not nearest-neighbor reduction, phase parametrization, positivity, or even the idea of a modular count. The supported distinct result is the structural odd-numerator collapse of the two frequencies to one rectangle count, coupled with an explicit uniform comparison to the nonresonant density by the square phase-lattice geometry. The inspected prior work does not give those conclusions; the related Resultary record concerns a different iterate and statistic. Review does not assert exhaustive priority.
